==English==
{{was wotd|2010|April|4|2011|April|4}}
{{wp|<dab>}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|witnesse|witneße||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|witnesse}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġewitnes}}, equivalent to {{af|en|wit|-ness}}. Cognate with {{cog|dum|wetenisse|t=witness, testimony}}, {{cog|goh|gewiznessi|t=testimony}}, {{cog|is|vitni|t=witness}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈwɪt.nɪs/|a=RP,GA,[[w:weak vowel merger|without weak vowel merger]]}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-witness.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈwɪt.nəs/|a=GA,AU,[[w:weak vowel merger|weak vowel merger]]}}
** {{audio|en|en-au-witness.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{hyph|en|wit|ness}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪtnəs|ɪtnɪs|s1=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[attestation|Attestation]] of a [[fact]] or [[event]]; [[testimony]].
#: {{ux|en|She can bear '''witness''', since she was there at the time.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|IV|ii|text=May we, with the warrant of womanhood and the '''witness''' of a good conscience, pursue him with any further revenge?}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=Expositions of holy scripture|volume=6|url=https://books.google.com/books?isbn=1610251350|author=Alexander MacLaren|year=1959
|passage=We have as much '''witness''' from heaven as we need.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=A Comprehensive Guide for Caregivers in Day-care Settings|url=https://books.google.com/books?isbn=0398083347|author=Nettie Becker; Paul Becker|year=1999
|passage=On another corner, stands an old style tenement building, whose dirty grey facade bears as much '''witness''' to the volume of exhaust fumes from millions of passing cars as it does to the age of the dwelling.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=The Excellency of Holy Courage in Evil Times|page=100|url=https://books.google.com/books?isbn=1937466167|author=Jeremiah Burroughs; C. Matthew McMahon; Therese B. McMahon|year=2008
|passage=Fleeing is giving '''witness''', and those that plead against it are loath to give so much '''witness'''}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} One who sees or has [[personal]] [[knowledge]] of something.
#: {{ux|en|As a '''witness''' to the event, I can confirm that he really said that.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Two Gentlemen of Verona|IV|ii|text={{...}}thyself art '''witness'''— I am betrothed.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1786|author={{w|Robert Hall (minister)|Robert Hall}}|title=A Reverie|text=Upon my looking round, I was a '''witness''' to appearances which filled me with melancholy and regret.}}
#* {{RQ:Bramah Bravo of London|passage=Joolby saw that Mr. Bronsky had looked in by another door and been a '''witness''' of the last stage of the quarrel}}
# {{lb|en|countable|law}} Someone called to give [[evidence]] in a [[court]].
#: {{ux|en|The '''witness''' for the prosecution did not seem very credible.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} One who is called upon to [[witness#Verb|witness]] an [[event]] or [[action]], such as a [[wedding]] or the [[sign]]ing of a [[document]].
#: {{ux|en|The bridesmaid and best man at a wedding typically serve as the '''witnesses'''.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} Something that serves as evidence; a [[sign]] or [[token]].
#* {{RQ:KJV|Genesis|31|51-52|text=Laban said to Jacob, {{...}} This heap be '''witness''', and this pillar be '''witness'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1918|author=James George Frazer|title=Folk-Lore In The Old Testament|volume=1|page=159|text=The bishop {{quote-gloss|Isidore}} was, as far as I am aware, the first off many writers who have appealed to fossil shells imbedded in remote mountains as '''witnesses''' to the truth of the Noachian tradition.}}
# {{lb|en|textual criticism}} A [[particular]] [[version]] of a [[text]] {{gloss|[[seen]] as providing [[testimony]] of [[archetype]] or other [[earlier]] [[version]]}}
# {{lb|en|countable|databases}} An additional [[database]] [[server]] [[instance]] used in [[failover]] [[scenario]]s to decide whether the [[mirror]] should [[take over]].

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[furnish]] [[proof]] of, to [[show]].
#: {{ux|en|This certificate '''witnesses''' his presence on that day.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=1|lines=56-57|passage=round he throws his baleful eyes / That '''witness'd''' huge affliction and dismay|year=1873}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To take as evidence.
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[see]] or gain knowledge of through experience.
#: {{ux|en|He '''witnessed''' the accident.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1801|author={{w|Robert Hall (minister)|Robert Hall}}|title=On Modern Infidelity|text=This is but a faint sketch of the incalculable calamities and horrors we must expect, should we be so unfortunate as ever to '''witness''' the triumph of modern infidelity}}
#* {{RQ:J. Marshall Washington|text=General Washington did not live to '''witness''' the restoration of peace.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|construed with '''to''' or '''for'''}} To present personal [[religious]] [[testimony]]; to [[preach]] at (someone) or on behalf of.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1998|section="Niebuhr, Reinhold"|title=Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy|volume=6|page=842|text=Instead, Niebuhr's God was the God '''witnessed''' to in the Hebrew Scriptures and the New Testament, the Bible of the Christian world.}}
# To see the [[execution]] of (a legal instrument), and [[subscribe]] it for the purpose of establishing its [[authenticity]].
#: {{ux|en|to '''witness''' a bond or a deed}}
